etymologies.etymologyHTML: From late Middle English comered, from Middle French camarade, from Spanish camarada or Italian camerata, from Medieval Latin *camarata, from Latin camara, camera (“a chamber”); see chamber. Compare camaraderie.

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XIII, page 20:
quote.text: [… these tears] Which weep the comrade of my choice,⁠An awful thought, a life removed,⁠The human-hearted man I loved,A spirit, not a breathing voice.

definitions.definition: A companion in battle; fellow soldier.

quote.citation: 2019, Antony Beevor, chapter 16, in Arnhem: The Battle for the Bridges, 1944, Penguin Books, page 194:
quote.text: Wierzbowski and his men were so exhausted that they could hardly stay awake, but they knew they could not abandon their wounded comrades.

definitions.definition: (communism) A fellow socialist, communist or other similarly politically aligned person.
(communism) A non-hierarchical title, functionally similar to "Mr.", "Mrs.", "Miss", "Ms." etc, in a communist or socialist state.
(intransitive) To associate with someone in a friendly way.

quote.text: But she was happy, for she was far away under another sky, and comrading again with her Rangers, and her animal friends, and the soldiers.
